input: SC-WOW-RES-001 — WoW resurrection range (as SC-GOT-MTN-001). Illidan restored; Sylvanas worn down; ghouls as tools. # SC-WOW-RES-001: the resurrection range in Warcraft (Game of Thrones style, SC-GOT-MTN-001)

SC-GOT-MTN-001 recorded a range in Game of Thrones: Jon comes back as himself, Beric loses a little each time, the Mountain comes back as a tool. Warcraft has the same range and four kinds the show lacks. Layers: CANON (game by patch), NOVEL, TRADITION, COMPILER. Consent is checked with SC-CONSENT-001's four conditions (voluntary, informed, agency kept, revocable).

## The range
| Case | How they return | Self kept | Consent | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scourge ghouls and the rank and file | plague and the Lich King's will (Warcraft III; Classic) | none | none | tools; freed only by destruction |
| Alexandros Mograine | taken to Naxxramas; his will broken by Kel'Thuzad (Ashbringer comic) | lost | none | a righteous man made a Horseman |
| Kel'Thuzad | killed by Arthas, raised as a lich at the Sunwell (Warcraft III) | full | he had served willingly | serves the Lich King, later the Jailer (Sanctum of Domination, 9.1) |
| The Death Knights of Acherus | raised as the Lich King's knights; freed at Light's Hope Chapel when he sacrificed them and Tirion Fordring intervened (3.0) | regained | none at entry; exit by betrayal and rescue | keep the power; serve Bolvar's Lich King by choice (7.0) |
| The new Four Horsemen | Darion Mograine, Thoras Trollbane, Nazgrim and Sally Whitemane raised by the Ebon Blade on Bolvar's order: "Salvation will come at a price the living cannot pay" (7.0) | kept | not asked | the liberated become raisers |
| The Forsaken | free will returned as the Lich King's power waned (Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne) | regained, changed | none at entry; freedom not chosen but given by circumstance | a people; then Sylvanas raises more with her val'kyr (Silverpine, 4.0) |
| Sylvanas Windrunner | killed by Arthas and raised as a banshee (Warcraft III); her own death at Icecrown and the Jailer's pact (Edge of Night, NOVEL; Legion) | kept, worn down | her pact chosen, not informed | sentenced to free, one by one, the souls she sent to the Maw (9.2) |
| Arthas | not raised; the first soul Frostmourne claimed was his own (Arthas: Rise of the Lich King, NOVEL) | lost | chose the blade, uninformed | killed in Icecrown Citadel (3.3) |
| Bolvar Fordragon | survived the Wrathgate's fire; took the Helm: "There must always be a Lich King" (3.3) | kept | voluntary and informed; not revocable while the Helm stood | released when Sylvanas shattered the Helm (9.0) |
| Illidan | soul held by Maiev; restored to his body (Legion, 7.1.5) | full | restored by allies | chooses to remain as Sargeras's jailer (7.3) |
| Nefarian and Onyxia | raised as undead in Blackwing Descent (4.0) | partial | none (Onyxia) | killed again |
| Calia Menethil | a Forsaken who wields the Light (Battle for Azeroth) | full | — | the Light inside undeath |
| Belo'ren, Child of Al'ar | a phoenix, born of Kael'thas's Al'ar (March on Quel'Danas, 12.0) | — | — | rebirth as a creature's nature, not an imposed return |

## What the range shows
1. The same axis as Game of Thrones: from a restored self (Illidan, like Jon) through a self worn down (Sylvanas, like Beric) to a tool (ghouls, the original Horsemen, like the Mountain).
2. Four kinds the show lacks. The voluntary vessel (Bolvar) takes the binding on himself to hold others. The liberated vessel keeps the binder's power (Death Knights). The liberated become binders (the Ebon Blade raising the new Horsemen; Sylvanas raising new Forsaken): the freed repeat the act they were freed from. The Light inside undeath (Calia; Sir Zeliek, who could still wield the Light in Naxxramas) breaks the rule that undeath and the Light cannot meet.
3. Freedom is mostly given, not taken. The Forsaken were freed by the Lich King's weakness; the Death Knights by his betrayal and Tirion's intervention. Only Bolvar's and Illidan's choices are fully their own.
4. The sentence for Sylvanas is restitution, not death (9.2): the one who raised others without consent is made to return them.

## Tradition (candidates)
- Raising the dead against their will: 1 Sam 28:7-19; Samuel, brought up at Endor, asks "Why hast thou disquieted me, to bring me up?" (28:15). The prohibition: Deut 18:10-12. Candidate for the Scourge and the Horsemen; difference: Samuel is not enslaved.
- Restoration to the same life: John 11:43-44 (Lazarus). Candidate for Illidan's return; difference: Illidan's return is the work of allies and a jailer, not a word.
- The new body: 1 Cor 15:42-44. No Warcraft case matches; recorded as absent.
- Freed and choosing to serve: Exod 21:5-6. Candidate for the Death Knights under Bolvar and Bolvar himself.
- Restitution: Luke 19:8 (Zacchaeus restores fourfold). Candidate for Sylvanas's sentence.
- A people raised by breath: Ezek 37:1-14. Weak for the Forsaken; the bones are raised whole and by God's spirit, the Forsaken are not.
- The phoenix as a resurrection figure: 1 Clement 25 (early Christian use of the phoenix). Candidate for Belo'ren; tradition, not scripture.

outputs.literal_translation:
Speaker [Shax/Curtis Kingsley] (t594u) asks for all of Warcraft through theology; the brief asks for a resurrection range in the Game of Thrones style.
Canon check: Death Knights freed at Light's Hope; Forsaken freed by the Lich King's weakness; Arthas not raised.
Residuals: freedom given, not taken.
outputs.public_translation: Warcraft has every kind of coming back: whole, worn down, or as a mindless tool. It adds a man who takes on a terrible binding to protect others, freed knights who keep the power, and freed people who then raise others without asking. None of this is a claim about the real world.

Sylvanas's sentence is to free the souls she sent to the Maw (9.2). Secondary source: Warcraft Wiki citing the game and novels.
